paragraphs: Wisdom sits at the door of whoever rises early, and goes about looking for the worthy. The psalmist answers with his refrain, “My soul is thirsting for you, O Lord my God,” and a memory that keeps him awake through the night watches. Such waiting is desire, not idleness. Paul says what it waits for: the Lord himself descending, the sleeping raised first, all of us together with him, and no one grieving as though without hope.

The ten virgins put that watch to the test, and all of them sleep. The difference is what each vessel holds. Augustine says it is charity, because oil rides above every liquid: “{{quote}}” Thomas à Kempis adds that love, even while sleeping, keeps watch.

Love cannot be borrowed at midnight; it is formed beforehand, in ordinary hours. Forgive a debt. Call the person who is grieving. Pray when the prayer is dry, as the psalmist thirsted in a dry land. Give someone an hour they cannot repay. Do it quietly and often, and the midnight cry will sound like a friend’s step.

quote.text: If you keep the usual order, it will be uppermost; if you change the order, it will be uppermost. Charity never falls.
quote.attribution: St Augustine, Sermon 43 on the New Testament Lessons (Ben. 93), on Matthew 25:1–13, §5
quote.translation: Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers, series 1, vol. 6 (ed. P. Schaff)
